newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND EXPECTS PLN 2.5 BLN IN 1997 PRIVATISATIONS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND EXPECTS PLN 2.5 BLN IN 1997 PRIVATISATIONS.

text.p: Poland is expecting to earn 2.5 billion zlotys from capital privatisations next year, against this year's 1.8 billion zlotys, deputy privatisation minister Jan Czekaj said on Monday.
Czekaj told reporters after a meeting of cabinet economic ministers (KERM) the revenue could rise to three billion zlotys if planned sales of financial institutions are completed.

"Revenue form capital privatisation in 1997 is likely to be 2.5 billion zlotys but this is not the final figure," Czekaj said. He said it could increase through direct privatisations of some 3,000 small companies.
"There are three thousand small companies which should undergo direct privatisation," Czekaj said.
Direct privatisation is a simplified form of capital privatisation, which requires elaborate formal procedures including an estimation of share capital and the firm's value.

Czekaj said the privatisation ministry would also turn about 240 state-run companies into treasury-owned joint-stock firms, thus submitting them to the commercial code in the first step towards their privatisation.
The government may also start next year the process of reprivatisation and create pension funds, if parliament passes appropriate laws.

Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek told reporters before the KERM meeting that revenues from privatisation next year could reach six billion zlotys and that it would encompass "sensitive" sectors of the economy, such as telecommunications, energy, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and distilleries.
